The header also holds what the run took in before recording started: a snapshot of every save store the doors opened (``saves``), the descriptors of devices opened (``devices``) and the enumeration answers given (``device_enumeration``). Then ``RecordingSources`` are installed around the active doors and record every frame from what passes through them (glitchygames/recording.py). SIGTERM (and SIGHUP on Unix, SIGBREAK on Windows) ends a started run through the normal teardown (``exit_on_signal``, installed by ``start``), and so does SIGINT (KeyboardInterrupt). ``stop_trace_recording`` (called by ``_shutdown``) closes the file. Recording must start before the first frame: afterwards installing its doors raises ``SourcesAlreadyRunningError`` (from ``install_sources``; glitchygames/sources.py). Args: path: The recording's file. Returns: The recorder. Raises: TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError: If this engine is already recording. """ if self . trace_recorder is not None : message = ( f 'start_trace_recording() was called while recording to ' f ' { self . trace_recorder . path } ; one run records once' ) raise TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError ( message ) inner = active_sources () registry = inner . devices () # A store a run started with --record-trace opened before recording started is in the # header as first opened: the first scene's setup() may have written to it since, and # the replay runs that setup() again (LiveSources.first_open_save_snapshots) first_open_snapshots : Mapping [ str , dict [ str , Any ]] = ( inner . first_open_save_snapshots if isinstance ( inner , LiveSources ) else {} ) # A rebaseline copies these fields from the replayed recording instead (rebaseline.py) header = { ** self . trace_recording_header (), SAVES_HEADER_FIELD : { namespace : ( first_open_snapshots [ namespace ] if namespace in first_open_snapshots else save_namespace_snapshot ( saves = store ) ) for namespace , store in inner . opened_save_namespaces . items () }, DEVICES_HEADER_FIELD : [ descriptor . to_json () for descriptor in registry . take_opened_descriptors () ], DEVICE_ENUMERATION_FIELD : [ answer . to_json () for answer in registry . take_enumeration_answers () ], } recorder = GameplayRecorder ( path = path , header = header ) install_sources ( sources = RecordingSources ( inner = inner , recorder = recorder )) self . trace_recorder = recorder self . log . info ( 'Recording gameplay to %s (random seed %s )' , path , self . random_seed ) return recorder

docs.text: Describe every unhandled event type, most frequent first. Each line names the type (pygame's event name and its number, so custom and unknown types still show), its count, when it was first seen and the first event's attribute names, e.g. JOYDEVICEADDED (1541) x1, first at 0.3 s, attributes: device_index, guid . Returns: list [ str ] – One line per type; empty when every event was handled. Source code in glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 3256 3257 3258 3259 3260 3261 3262 3263 3264 3265 3266 3267 3268 3269 3270 3271 3272 3273 3274 3275 3276 3277 def unhandled_event_report ( self : Self ) -> list [ str ]: """Describe every unhandled event type, most frequent first. Each line names the type (pygame's event name and its number, so custom and unknown types still show), its count, when it was first seen and the first event's attribute names, e.g. ``JOYDEVICEADDED (1541) x1, first at 0.3 s, attributes: device_index, guid``. Returns: One line per type; empty when every event was handled. """ records = sorted ( self . unhandled_events . items (), key = lambda item : item [ 1 ] . count , reverse = True , ) return [ f ' { pygame . event . event_name ( event_type ) . upper () } ( { event_type } ) x { record . count } , ' f 'first at { record . first_seen_seconds : .1f } s, ' f 'attributes: { ", " . join ( record . attribute_names ) or "none" } ' for event_type , record in records ]

docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). docs.text: End the run with SystemExit, so GameEngine.start()'s teardown still runs. Installed by GameEngine.start for each of terminating_signals() that nothing else handles, for the whole run, so a recording is closed by _shutdown . It ignores further signals of the same kind before raising: a second SIGTERM ( uv run forwards one to its child as well, and pkill can match both) would otherwise raise again inside the teardown and leave the recording unclosed. _shutdown restores the default handling after closing the recording. It does nothing else: logging here could fail with "reentrant call" if the signal interrupted a write to the same stream. Parameters: signal_number ( int ) – The signal received. _frame ( FrameType | None ) – The interrupted frame (unused). Raises: SystemExit – Always, with ExitCode.for_signal(signal_number) ( TERMINATED for SIGTERM, HANGUP for SIGHUP, BREAK for SIGBREAK). Source code in glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 277 278 279 280 281 282 283 284 285 286 287 288 289 290 291 292 293 294 295 296 297 298 def exit_on_signal ( signal_number : int , _frame : FrameType | None ) -> None : """End the run with SystemExit, so GameEngine.start()'s teardown still runs. Installed by ``GameEngine.start`` for each of ``terminating_signals()`` that nothing else handles, for the whole run, so a recording is closed by ``_shutdown``. It ignores further signals of the same kind before raising: a second SIGTERM (``uv run`` forwards one to its child as well, and ``pkill`` can match both) would otherwise raise again inside the teardown and leave the recording unclosed. ``_shutdown`` restores the default handling after closing the recording. It does nothing else: logging here could fail with "reentrant call" if the signal interrupted a write to the same stream. Args: signal_number: The signal received. _frame: The interrupted frame (unused). Raises: SystemExit: Always, with ``ExitCode.for_signal(signal_number)`` (``TERMINATED`` for SIGTERM, ``HANGUP`` for SIGHUP, ``BREAK`` for SIGBREAK). """ signal . signal ( signal_number , signal . SIG_IGN ) raise SystemExit ( ExitCode . for_signal ( signal_number ))

A ResourceManager subclass will generally pass all requests through to its proxy object(s), however, for certain types of resources such as joysticks, the subclass will manage things itself. This architecture reduces code footprint, and allows maxium flexibility when needed, at the expense of a bit of abstraction. docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 457 458 459 460 461 462 463 464 465 466 467 468 469 470 471 472 473 474 475 476 477 478 479 480 481 482 483 484 485 486 487 488 489 490 491 492 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 1312 1313 1314 1315 1316 1317 1318 1319 1320 1321 1322 1323 1324 1325 1326 1327 1328 1329 1330 1331 1332 1333 1334 1335 1336 1337 1338 1339 1340 1341 1342 1343 1344 1345 1346 1347 1348 1349 1350 1351 1352 1353 1354 1355 1356 @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 1312 1313 1314 1315 1316 1317 1318 1319 1320 1321 1322 1323 1324 1325 1326 1327 1328 1329 1330 1331 1332 1333 1334 1335 1336 1337 1338 1339 1340 1341 1342 1343 1344 1345 1346 1347 1348 1349 1350 1351 1352 1353 1354 1355 1356 @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, with_fields ) computes its own. Returns: int ( int ) – The hash value. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 802 803 804 805 806 807 808 809 810 811 812 813 814 815 816 817 818 819 820 821 822 823 824 825 826 827 828 829 830 @override def __hash__ ( self : Self ) -> int : """Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, ``with_fields``) computes its own. Returns: int: The hash value. """ content_hash : int | None = self . _content_hash if content_hash is not None : return content_hash # Guard against infinite recursion when __dict__ contains this event (as __eq__ does); # the inner call's stand-in is never cached self_id = id ( self ) if self_id in HashableEvent . _hashing_ids : return hash ( self . type ) HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . add ( self_id ) try : content_hash = hash ( frozenset (( name , _hashable_value ( value )) for name , value in self . __dict__ . items ()) ) finally : HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . discard ( self_id ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( self , content_hash ) return content_hash

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 457 458 459 460 461 462 463 464 465 466 467 468 469 470 471 472 473 474 475 476 477 478 479 480 481 482 483 484 485 486 487 488 489 490 491 492 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

docs.text: Wrap a pygame event, as its type's class ( EVENT_CLASSES ): the engine's dispatch. The same event the constructor builds ( HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict) ), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 457 458 459 460 461 462 463 464 465 466 467 468 469 470 471 472 473 474 475 476 477 478 479 480 481 482 483 484 485 486 487 488 489 490 491 492 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

""" # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

The same event the constructor builds ( HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict) ), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 457 458 459 460 461 462 463 464 465 466 467 468 469 470 471 472 473 474 475 476 477 478 479 480 481 482 483 484 485 486 487 488 489 490 491 492 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

docs.text: Wrap a pygame event, as its type's class ( EVENT_CLASSES ): the engine's dispatch. The same event the constructor builds ( HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict) ), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. Parameters: pygame_event ( Event ) – The raw event. Returns: HashableEvent ( HashableEvent ) – The event. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 506 507 508 509 510 511 512 513 514 515 516 517 518 519 520 521 522 523 524 525 526 527 @staticmethod def from_pygame ( pygame_event : pygame . event . Event ) -> HashableEvent : """Wrap a pygame event, as its type's class (``EVENT_CLASSES``): the engine's dispatch. The same event the constructor builds (``HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict)``), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. Args: pygame_event: The raw event. Returns: HashableEvent: The event. """ event_type = pygame_event . type event = object . __new__ ( EVENT_CLASSES . get ( event_type , HashableEvent )) fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = event_type fields . update ( pygame_event . dict ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) return event

ABC ): """Abstract base class for event interfaces.""" log : ClassVar [ logging . Logger ] = LOG # Declared here so EventStubs satisfy GameOptionsProvider when passed to # unhandled_event(). At runtime, the concrete class (Scene/GameEngine) # provides the real options dict via the ResourceManager singleton chain. options : dict [ str , Any ] @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). docs.text: Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, with_fields ) computes its own. Returns: int ( int ) – The hash value. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 802 803 804 805 806 807 808 809 810 811 812 813 814 815 816 817 818 819 820 821 822 823 824 825 826 827 828 829 830 @override def __hash__ ( self : Self ) -> int : """Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, ``with_fields``) computes its own. Returns: int: The hash value. """ content_hash : int | None = self . _content_hash if content_hash is not None : return content_hash # Guard against infinite recursion when __dict__ contains this event (as __eq__ does); # the inner call's stand-in is never cached self_id = id ( self ) if self_id in HashableEvent . _hashing_ids : return hash ( self . type ) HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . add ( self_id ) try : content_hash = hash ( frozenset (( name , _hashable_value ( value )) for name , value in self . __dict__ . items ()) ) finally : HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . discard ( self_id ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( self , content_hash ) return content_hash

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 457 458 459 460 461 462 463 464 465 466 467 468 469 470 471 472 473 474 475 476 477 478 479 480 481 482 483 484 485 486 487 488 489 490 491 492 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )
docs.title: __new__

UserDict's own ``|`` read ``self.data``, which this class never sets, so it raised AttributeError. Returns: Self: The changed copy, or NotImplemented when ``other`` is not a mapping. The event is rebuilt from the state's attributes exactly as init builds it, so it equals and hashes like the event the state came from (BUGS.md #121: this hashed a dict). docs.text: Wrap a pygame event, as its type's class ( EVENT_CLASSES ): the engine's dispatch. The same event the constructor builds ( HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict) ), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. Event ) -> HashableEvent : """Wrap a pygame event, as its type's class (``EVENT_CLASSES``): the engine's dispatch. The same event the constructor builds (``HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict)``), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. Args: pygame_event: The raw event. Returns: HashableEvent: The event. """ event_type = pygame_event . type event = object . __new__ ( EVENT_CLASSES . get ( event_type , HashableEvent )) fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = event_type fields . update ( pygame_event . dict ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) return event

docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 1312 1313 1314 1315 1316 1317 1318 1319 1320 1321 1322 1323 1324 1325 1326 1327 1328 1329 1330 1331 1332 1333 1334 1335 1336 1337 1338 1339 1340 1341 1342 1343 1344 1345 1346 1347 1348 1349 1350 1351 1352 1353 1354 1355 1356 @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. docs.text: Bases: UserDict [ str , Any ] Hashable, immutable event class. Hashable events are cacheable, so we can mitigate some of the performance overhead of glitchygames' event subsystem by caching events, which will result in an immediate return if an identical event is encountered, saving some function overhead and processing. Games are welcome to use the built-in pygame event subsystem, but on_*_event callbacks will not be available in that case. The class is chosen by the event's type: HashableEvent(pygame.MOUSEMOTION, ...) builds a MouseMotionEvent ( EVENT_CLASSES ), so every event of a type is an instance of that type's class however it was built; custom and unknown types stay HashableEvent . The per-type classes only declare their fields (for the type checker): they store, hash, compare, pickle and serialize exactly as this class does. Equality is by type and fields, never by Python class. An event never changes after construction (it is hashed, and its hash is cached): item and attribute assignment, deletion, update , clear , pop , popitem , setdefault and |= raise TypeError; with_fields(**changes) returns a changed copy. Field values should be immutable too: a list or dict inside a game event is hashed by its contents once, so changing it afterwards leaves the cached hash stale. The per-type classes only declare their fields (for the type checker): they store, hash, compare, pickle and serialize exactly as this class does. Equality is by type and fields, never by Python class. An event never changes after construction (it is hashed, and its hash is cached): item and attribute assignment, deletion, ``update``, ``clear``, ``pop``, ``popitem``, ``setdefault`` and ``|=`` raise TypeError; ``with_fields(**changes)`` returns a changed copy. Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event ) if TYPE_CHECKING : # The constructor's signature for the type checker (UserDict's __init__ takes a # mapping); at run time __init__ is object's def __init__ ( self , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> None : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Declare the constructor's arguments (``__new__`` builds the event).""" else : # Everything is done in __new__; object's __init__ accepts the constructor's arguments # (a class that overrides __new__ but not __init__) and does nothing, without a second # Python call per event __init__ = object . __init__ @staticmethod def from_pygame ( pygame_event : pygame . event . docs.text: Wrap a pygame event, as its type's class ( EVENT_CLASSES ): the engine's dispatch. The same event the constructor builds ( HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict) ), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. The same event the constructor builds (``HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict)``), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. Args: pygame_event: The raw event. Returns: HashableEvent: The event. """ event_type = pygame_event . type event = object . __new__ ( EVENT_CLASSES . get ( event_type , HashableEvent )) fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = event_type fields . update ( pygame_event . dict ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) return event

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 457 458 459 460 461 462 463 464 465 466 467 468 469 470 471 472 473 474 475 476 477 478 479 480 481 482 483 484 485 486 487 488 489 490 491 492 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 457 458 459 460 461 462 463 464 465 466 467 468 469 470 471 472 473 474 475 476 477 478 479 480 481 482 483 484 485 486 487 488 489 490 491 492 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

docs.text: Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, with_fields ) computes its own. Returns: int ( int ) – The hash value. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 802 803 804 805 806 807 808 809 810 811 812 813 814 815 816 817 818 819 820 821 822 823 824 825 826 827 828 829 830 @override def __hash__ ( self : Self ) -> int : """Return the hash of the event's content (its type and fields), cached. Equal events hash alike however they were built. Unhashable values (a game event's lists and dicts) hash by their content. Computed on the first call and kept in a slot (never a field); a copy (pickled, ``with_fields``) computes its own. Returns: int: The hash value. """ content_hash : int | None = self . _content_hash if content_hash is not None : return content_hash # Guard against infinite recursion when __dict__ contains this event (as __eq__ does); # the inner call's stand-in is never cached self_id = id ( self ) if self_id in HashableEvent . _hashing_ids : return hash ( self . type ) HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . add ( self_id ) try : content_hash = hash ( frozenset (( name , _hashable_value ( value )) for name , value in self . __dict__ . items ()) ) finally : HashableEvent . _hashing_ids . discard ( self_id ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( self , content_hash ) return content_hash

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 457 458 459 460 461 462 463 464 465 466 467 468 469 470 471 472 473 474 475 476 477 478 479 480 481 482 483 484 485 486 487 488 489 490 491 492 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

docs.text: Wrap a pygame event, as its type's class ( EVENT_CLASSES ): the engine's dispatch. The same event the constructor builds ( HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict) ), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. Parameters: pygame_event ( Event ) – The raw event. Returns: HashableEvent ( HashableEvent ) – The event. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 506 507 508 509 510 511 512 513 514 515 516 517 518 519 520 521 522 523 524 525 526 527 @staticmethod def from_pygame ( pygame_event : pygame . event . Event ) -> HashableEvent : """Wrap a pygame event, as its type's class (``EVENT_CLASSES``): the engine's dispatch. The same event the constructor builds (``HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict)``), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. Args: pygame_event: The raw event. Returns: HashableEvent: The event. """ event_type = pygame_event . type event = object . __new__ ( EVENT_CLASSES . get ( event_type , HashableEvent )) fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = event_type fields . update ( pygame_event . dict ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) return event

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 457 458 459 460 461 462 463 464 465 466 467 468 469 470 471 472 473 474 475 476 477 478 479 480 481 482 483 484 485 486 487 488 489 490 491 492 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 1312 1313 1314 1315 1316 1317 1318 1319 1320 1321 1322 1323 1324 1325 1326 1327 1328 1329 1330 1331 1332 1333 1334 1335 1336 1337 1338 1339 1340 1341 1342 1343 1344 1345 1346 1347 1348 1349 1350 1351 1352 1353 1354 1355 1356 @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 1312 1313 1314 1315 1316 1317 1318 1319 1320 1321 1322 1323 1324 1325 1326 1327 1328 1329 1330 1331 1332 1333 1334 1335 1336 1337 1338 1339 1340 1341 1342 1343 1344 1345 1346 1347 1348 1349 1350 1351 1352 1353 1354 1355 1356 @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to ( EVENT_CLASSES ). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here ( __init__ is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Parameters: type ( int ) – The type of the event. *_args ( Any , default: () ) – Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes ( Any , default: {} ) – The event's fields. Returns: Self ( Self ) – An instance of the type's class: HashableEvent (or the class called) for Self – a type with no class of its own. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 457 458 459 460 461 462 463 464 465 466 467 468 469 470 471 472 473 474 475 476 477 478 479 480 481 482 483 484 485 486 487 488 489 490 491 492 def __new__ ( cls , type : int , * _args : Any , ** attributes : Any ) -> Self : # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] """Create a hashable event, as the class its type maps to (``EVENT_CLASSES``). Pygames events are not hashable by default. All of the construction happens here (``__init__`` is object's): one Python call per event, which matters for mouse-motion floods. A per-type class called with a type it cannot hold (another family's, or a type without a class of its own) raises ValueError. Args: type: The type of the event. *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused). **attributes: The event's fields. Returns: Self: An instance of the type's class: ``HashableEvent`` (or the class called) for a type with no class of its own. """ type_class = EVENT_CLASSES . get ( type ) if type_class is None : event_class = cls if cls not in _TYPED_EVENT_CLASSES else _refused_class ( cls , type ) elif cls is HashableEvent or cls is type_class : event_class = type_class else : event_class = _event_class_for ( cls = cls , event_type = type , type_class = type_class ) event = object . __new__ ( event_class ) # The event's attributes are exactly its type and fields: nothing else is stored in # __dict__ (a stored hash there showed up as a field, BUGS.md #179). Written through # __dict__ because attribute assignment raises (the event is immutable); the cached # hash is None until the first __hash__ fields = event . __dict__ fields [ 'type' ] = type fields . update ( attributes ) _CONTENT_HASH_SLOT . __set__ ( event , None ) # event_class is cls or one of its subclasses, so the event is a Self return cast ( 'Self' , event )

The same event the constructor builds ( HashableEvent(pygame_event.type, **pygame_event.dict) ), without unpacking the fields into keyword arguments twice: every dispatched event comes through here, mouse-motion floods included. docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (callable)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> implemented (attribute)' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( ' %s . %s -> unimplemented' , subclass . __name__ , attribute ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented
