docs.text: Exact replay of a --record-trace recording through the real engine ( --replay-trace ). ReplaySources are the doors (glitchygames/sources.py) a replay installs: everything the recorded run took in is served from the recording, so the real engine and game code run the session again, and every frame's sprites are compared with the recorded frame. The rules (plans/2026-10-19-gameplay-replay.md, sections 3.1-3.3): Startup, in one place ( GameEngine.__init__ ): once the options are parsed, start_replay reads the recording, refuses a recording of another game ( ReplayRefusedError ; the engine logs it and exits with ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT , as for an unreadable file or a malformed one ( decoded_replay_sources ), or ExitCode.MISSING_INPUT for a missing one; glitchygames/exit_codes.py), warns once about a different engine version, applies the recorded options (all but REPLAY_LOCAL_OPTIONS ) and seeds the random streams with the recorded seed. Games read the display's size, so the window opens at the header's screen_size (the size the recorded display had, which a window manager may have made other than the recorded --resolution ): apply_recorded_screen_size sets the resolution option to it, and the engine's normal display set-up opens it (headless or watched). A window that still opens at another size is refused ( display_size_refusal : the engine logs Cannot replay PATH: it was recorded on a 800x600 display, but the window opened at 800x480 ... and exits with ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT ); a screen_size that is not two positive integers is a malformed header ( UNUSABLE_INPUT ). A header without one (not written by the engine's recorder, which always writes it, format 2 included) keeps the recorded --resolution , with a warning. A size that changes during the recorded run is not recorded, so a game that reads the live size every frame can still diverge. The engine installs the sources before the first frame; while installed they own the internal-post tracker (glitchygames/recording.py). Pump: the real queue is drained (through the live doors' pump) and each event classified with the internal-post tracker. From the first drain on, real input, device and window events are blocked at SDL ( REAL_INPUT_EVENT_TYPES , glitchygames/replay/input_blocking.py), so they never enter the queue (each drain blocks them again, as an event manager made mid-run allows its types); the blocked state each type had before comes back when the replay ends ( finish_run , normally or after an error) or is uninstalled. QUIT, the window's close event and the custom range are never blocked, nor, in a watched replay, are KEYDOWN and KEYUP ( WATCHED_REAL_KEY_EVENT_TYPES : the viewer's keys, rule 14). Blocking also refuses posts of those types: game code that fakes input by posting, say, KEYDOWN loses the post, which shows as a missing internal event divergence (the engine's own posts are QUIT and custom types). So game code posting KEYDOWN or KEYUP replays differently watched and headless: watched, the keys are not blocked, the post arrives and matches its recorded internal record; headless (and so --audit ), it is refused and diverges. A recording of such a game can match watched and diverge headless. What external events still arrive (queued before the first drain, the close event, app lifecycle and system notifications) never reach the game: a watched replay's real key presses and releases go to its controls (rule 14), the rest are dropped, except the window's QUIT, kept last so closing the window ends the replay. A control tick of a held frame (rule 14) drains the queue the same way; the internal events it finds wait for the next pump. Pump N serves the recording's batch N in its recorded order: each external record is rebuilt (recorded references mapped to live objects: a window to None, as live events of the display module's window carry it; a joystick to its opened stand-in, an event whose joystick has none being dropped with one warning per instance id), and each internal record is the live internal event the replayed code posted again (equal records). A recorded internal event nobody posted, a posted one the recording does not have, or a frame pumped more or fewer times than recorded is a divergence of the frame. Internal events are matched by encoded record ( event_to_record ), so one carrying a window or joystick reference would compare the recorded and live ids; none of the engine's posts carry one today. Frame indexes: the sources count their own end_frame calls; every recorded frame they serve is picked by that count, never by the scene manager's frame number. Frame time: the current frame's recorded dt ; past the end, the measurement. The FPS events and performance statistics ( performance_frame_seconds ) use it too under --replay-fps recorded (the default), so the FPS events are compared exactly; under --replay-fps real they use this machine's measured frame time, and FPS events are not compared (logic still receives the recorded dt ). Input: the frame's snapshot, rebuilt by applying each frame's input_changes in order (a version-2 recording has none: polled input reads as idle, with one warning). Held keys answer by the key codes the recording machine held them as, whatever this machine's keyboard layout (glitchygames/input/state.py). Devices: a ReplayDeviceRegistry from the header, learning each frame's opened devices and enumeration answers when the frame begins (before any open in it is answered). Saves: a MemorySaveManager per namespace, seeded from the header's saves or the frame's saves_opened (an unknown namespace gets an empty store); real saves are never touched. End of frame: a divergence found by the frame's pumps comes first; then the frame's control events that are not applied again (markers the replayed code records by itself) are compared with the recorded ones, in order; then the scene's sprites are sampled as the recorder samples them and compared with the recorded frame (scene class, then each sprite: present, rect , visible ). The first difference stops a headless replay, as does the last recorded frame; a watched replay pauses there instead (rule 14). Under ReplayOptions.stop_on_divergence False ( --rebaseline , rule 17) a difference stops nothing: the result keeps the first one, counts the frames that differ ( ReplayResult.differing_frame_count ) and names every sprite that differs in them ( ReplayResult.affected_sprite_ids ), and the replay runs on to the last recorded frame. The report's history ends at the first divergent frame either way. A frame that pumped fewer times than recorded never serves its remaining batches (they are not carried into a later pump); their external events are counted ( ReplayResult.undelivered_input_count ). Clocks: the wall clock is the recording's recorded_at plus the frame clock; elapsed seconds are the frame clock, live and replayed alike (glitchygames/clock.py). recorded_frame_fields hands a recording made over the replay ( --rebaseline , rule 17) the frame's recorded saves and device fields, and last_batch_origins each event's origin in the batch the last pump returned. GameEngine._shutdown calls finish_run and reports the result ( ReplayResult.report : printed to stdout under --headless , logged otherwise); GameEngine.start then ends the run with ReplayResult.exit_code(policy=options.exit_policy) . The report of a sprite divergence lists the sprite in the last REPORT_HISTORY_FRAMES frames before it, recorded and replayed (kept by end_frame ). Digests ( --replay-digest PATH , for --audit : glitchygames/replay/audit.py): each compared frame's frame_digest (of the frame as sampled for rule 8) is kept, and finish_run writes them with the divergence summary to the digest file. The engine refuses a digest file it cannot write before the run ( ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT ); one that cannot be written at the end is logged on one line ( digest_write_failed ), and the run exits ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT once the replay is reported. Pacing: the scene manager never paces a replay ( paced_frame_seconds is 0.0). A headless replay ( --headless ) is not paced at all, as its frame times come from the recording. A watched replay is paced by its viewer (glitchygames/replay/viewer.py, whose docstring is the contract): an outer tick 60 times a second of real time ( glitchygames.clock.measured_seconds , never replayed: it only decides when frames run, never what they do) runs the inner recorded frames its accumulator pays for (real time times the speed, consumed by each frame's recorded duration, bounded per tick in frames and real time, never owing more than one tick's worth). Watching (not --headless ): ReplayControls (glitchygames/replay/controls.py) take the viewer's real key presses and releases; none reaches the game. hold_frame drives the viewer: with no outer tick open it sleeps until the next one, drains the real queue and acts on the keys read since the last tick (once per press; a key already down when the replay starts acts only after its release); it then answers False for each inner frame the open tick runs and True when the tick closes, refreshing the status line (showing the real speed while the viewer cannot keep up); the scene manager then presents that frame. Inner frames are not presented ( presents_frames is False). The start screen ( ReplayOptions.wait_for_start ) holds the loop after frame 0, so the first frame's picture is behind the message (frame 0's sounds play before Space, and a one-frame recording reaches its end at the start screen). The loop is also held while paused (until a step) and once the recording is used up. At a divergence or the end the replay pauses with the debug overlay on ( ReplayControls.debug_overlay , the scene manager's, handed over by the engine) and a banner ( ReplayControls.banner ) instead of stopping; Esc stops it (a run that already ended keeps its end reason, else 'quit' ). The status bar is drawn by draw_overlay . A headless replay never holds and has no controls' keys: its KEYDOWN and KEYUP stay blocked. Step back ( , ), Home and D restart the replay (glitchygames/replay/rebuild.py, whose docstring is the contract): a control tick that takes the controls' restart request ( ReplayControls.take_restart_request ) stops the replay with ReplayResult.restart_frame set and the end reason 'restart' , and the engine relaunches it once torn down. A replay given ReplayOptions.pause_at_frame N (watched only: a headless replay ignores it, as nobody could unpause it) rebuilds: without its start screen, frames run unpresented and unpaced in silence ( Rebuild.silence_frame after each; hold_frame never holds, except every REBUILD_PROGRESS_INTERVAL_SECONDS of real time to present the progress line and read the viewer's keys), until frame max(N, FIRST_PAUSED_FRAME) is the next to run; there it pauses. A divergence or the end of the recording on the way pauses it there instead (rule 14). ReplayOptions.viewer_state restores the viewer's speed, debug panel and the divergence frame an earlier run found. Bookmarks (watched): B bookmarks the frame the status line shows ( ReplayControls.bookmarks , frame N meaning paused with frame N next). S ( ReplaySources.bookmarks , saved by the control tick) writes a copy of the recording ( write_bookmarked_copy ) to bookmarked_copy_path , with a {'kind': 'breakpoint', 'label': 'bookmark'} control event appended to frame N - 1 (the frame whose picture was shown) for each bookmark N (one already there is not added again; other control events are kept). The same bookmarks as the last save are not written again (unless that copy was deleted since). The copy's header names its source ( bookmarked_copy_of ); only a file with that field is updated in place (written aside and moved in), so an original is never written, even one named like a copy, nor a copy of another recording; a copy an earlier session saved from the same source keeps its bookmarks (they are added to the viewer's). The copy replays as its source does: a cut-off source gives source_truncated (the copy ends as truncated) and a version-2 source input_capture_format_version (polled input reads as idle, markers are not compared). With no bookmarks nothing is written and the viewer is told so. A breakpoint is re-applied on its frame (glitchygames/supervision.py) and is not compared, so the copy replays exactly as the original; a watched replay pauses when it applies one ( ReplayControls.pause_at_breakpoint , a control event handler the engine registers), except while rebuilding, so a saved copy reopens and stops at each bookmark. A recording's bookmark breakpoints are the viewer's bookmarks from the start, so S keeps them. A restart (rule 15) with bookmarks saves the copy first and replays the copy ( GameEngine._restart_replay , which warns naming the bookmarks if the copy cannot be saved), so bookmarks survive step back. Rebaseline ( --replay-trace OLD --rebaseline NEW --headless ; glitchygames/replay/ rebaseline.py, whose docstring is the contract): start_replay gives the replay stop_on_divergence=False and ReplayExitPolicy.SUCCESS_AFTER_WRITING , and the engine records the run over it into NEW ( RecordingSources with replayed set: origins and the saves and device fields come from this replay, never from the live trackers). It also gives it captures_scene_starts=True , so the scenes the replayed code builds capture their starts and NEW holds them ( scene_start , frame 0's included), as a --record-trace recording does; a recording's scene_start fields are never compared (the replayed code captures its own). Playback (Part 3's in-game playback scope, glitchygames/replay/playback.py, whose docstring is the contract): playback_replay_sources builds the sources a scope serves a recording's frames from, starting at ReplayOptions.start_frame N (the frame holding the rebuilt scene's scene_start ). They behave as a headless replay's that nobody watches: no viewer, controls, start screen or overlay; they never hold, pause or pace (the scope uses the installed doors' pacing and presenting) and stop at the recording's end or first divergence; no game check, recorded options or seed are applied, and no report is printed and no exit code given (the scope keeps the result). The frames before N are not served: what they took in is learned when the sources are made (opened devices, saves first opened, the polled input they changed; not enumeration answers, which those frames consumed), and the sprite ids continue the recording's ( StableSpriteIds 's recorded_ids : the ids those frames gave, but those frame N holds, which are the replayed scene's own, sampled already between its setup and its first logic frame), so frame N is compared as recorded. Saves start from the scene start's save view, over the header's. The internal events of frame N's first batch that were posted before the scene began ( ReplayOptions.earlier_internal_event_count , from its start's first logic frame; glitchygames/scene_start.py, rule 7) are served from the recording, as external ones are, and not compared; so are the events frame N's redelivered_events holds (a playback scope's held events, delivered before its first pump: they belong to the frame, but no door pumped them), first in its first batch ( ReplayOptions.serves_redelivered_events ). Frame indexes stay the recording's (rule 3, offset by N): divergences name recording frames, and ReplayResult.frames_replayed counts up to the last compared recording frame. A later frame holding a resume_bridge (an instant-replay journal's: its scene resumed there after a playback scope; glitchygames/instant_replay.py, rule 7) begins as the start frame does: the bridge is kept for the frame ( frame_bridge : the playback scope sets the frame clock, the FPS event timer and the polled input from it at the top of the frame), the polled input before it is the bridge's, the first earlier_internal_event_count internal events of its first batch are served from the recording, uncompared, and its redelivered_events come first in its first pump: the external ones served, the internal ones (the scene's own posts from before the scope, which the playback ran) matched with the live posts. A frame's playback_answers are kept for the frame ( recorded_playback_answers ): the playback scope answers the replayed code's playback requests with them (glitchygames/replay/playback.py, answered_playback_request ).

Rule 16: S asks for a save (the control tick calls ``save``), and ``GameEngine._restart_replay`` saves before a restart with bookmarks. """ def __init__ ( self : Self , * , controls : ReplayControls , recording_path : Path | None , is_bookmarked_copy : bool , ) -> None : """Keep what a save needs. Args: controls: The watched replay's controls (their ``bookmarks``, and where the outcome is shown); their bookmarks start as the recording's own. recording_path: The file the recording was read from (``ReplayOptions.recording_path``), or None. is_bookmarked_copy: True when the recording is a bookmarked copy: its bookmarks are already saved in it. """ self . _controls = controls self . _recording_path = recording_path # The bookmarks last saved and where (a save of the same ones writes nothing) self . _saved_bookmarks : list [ int ] | None = None self . _saved_path : Path | None = None if is_bookmarked_copy and recording_path is not None : self . _saved_bookmarks = list ( controls . bookmarks ) self . _saved_path = recording_path def save ( self : Self ) -> Path | None : """Save a copy of the recording with the bookmarks as breakpoints. The viewer is told the outcome (``ReplayControls.show_message``), and it is logged. The same bookmarks as the last save (or as a bookmarked copy being replayed holds) are not written again, unless that copy has been deleted since. Returns: The copy's path (already saved, or just written), or None when there is no copy: no bookmarks, no recording file (sources made from frames in memory), or the copy could not be written. """ bookmarks = list ( self . _controls . bookmarks ) if not bookmarks : self . _controls . show_message ( text = NO_BOOKMARKS_MESSAGE ) return None if self . _recording_path is None : self . _controls . show_message ( text = NO_RECORDING_FILE_MESSAGE ) return None if ( self . _saved_path is not None and bookmarks == self . _saved_bookmarks # A copy deleted since it was saved is written again and self . _saved_path . exists () ): self . _controls . show_message ( text = ALREADY_SAVED_MESSAGE . format ( name = self . _saved_path . name ) ) return self . _saved_path destination = bookmarked_copy_path ( recording_path = self . _recording_path ) try : write_bookmarked_copy ( recording_path = self . _recording_path , bookmarks = bookmarks , destination = destination ) # A TraceFormatError (the file changed since it was read) is a ValueError except ( OSError , ValueError ) as error : LOG . exception ( 'Could not save bookmarks %s to %s ' , bookmarks , destination ) self . _controls . show_message ( text = f 'could not save bookmarks: { error } ' ) return None LOG . info ( 'Saved bookmarks %s to %s ' , bookmarks , destination ) self . _controls . show_message ( text = f 'bookmarks saved to { destination . name } ' ) self . _saved_bookmarks = bookmarks self . _saved_path = destination return destination

ReplaySources : """The replay's doors (implements glitchygames.sources.EngineSources; module docstring). Attributes: header: The recording's header fields (without ``format_version`` and ``frames``). recording: The recorded frames. options: How the replay is run (``ReplayOptions``). result: How the replay went so far. random_seed: The recorded master seed. controls: The watched replay's controls (rule 14; unused by a headless replay). viewer: The watched replay's outer loop (rule 14, glitchygames/replay/viewer.py). bookmarks: Saves the viewer's bookmarks into a copy of the recording (rule 16). draws_overlay: True for a watched replay, which draws its status bar (``draw_overlay``). presents_frames: False for a watched replay, whose viewer presents the latest frame once per outer tick. captures_scene_starts: Whether scenes built now capture their starts (``ReplayOptions.captures_scene_starts``: a rebaseline's). start_input: The polled input before the start frame (``IDLE_INPUT`` before frame 0), which the start frame's logic reads (``dt_tick`` runs before the frame's pump); a playback scope makes it the current input as it begins (rule 18). frame_bridge: The current frame's resume bridge, when the recorded scene resumed in it after a playback scope (an instant-replay journal's frame; rule 18), else None. recorded_playback_answers: The answers the current frame's playback requests got, not yet given again (an instant-replay journal's ``playback_answers``; rule 18). digest_write_failed: True once ``finish_run`` could not write the digest file (rule 12; the engine then exits ``ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT``). """ # Set for each frame as it begins (_begin_frame) frame_bridge : ResumeBridge | None recorded_playback_answers : collections . deque [ bool ] # Set by finish_run when the digest file cannot be written digest_write_failed : bool = False def __init__ ( self : Self , * , header : dict [ str , Any ], frames : Sequence [ dict [ str , Any ]], format_version : int , is_truncated : bool = False , options : ReplayOptions = DEFAULT_REPLAY_OPTIONS , ) -> None : """Prepare to serve the recording from its first frame. Args: header: The header fields. frames: Every complete recorded frame, decoded (glitchygames/tracing.py). format_version: The file's format version (2 or 3). is_truncated: True when the file was cut off (a killed recorder): the replay then ends with ``'truncated'`` after the last complete frame. options: How the replay is run. """ self . header = header self . options = options self . random_seed = _recorded_seed ( header = header ) self . _recorded_at = _recorded_start ( header = header ) # A bookmarked copy of a cut-off recording ends as its source did (rule 16) self . recording = RecordedFrames ( frames = frames , is_truncated = is_truncated or header . get ( SOURCE_TRUNCATED_HEADER_FIELD ) is True , ) self . result = ReplayResult ( frames_recorded = self . recording . frame_count , max_processing_slowdown_percent = options . max_processing_slowdown_percent , # Each frame's processing time beside the recorded one (replay/processing.py) processing_comparison = ( ProcessingComparison ( recorded_machine = _recorded_machine ( header = header ), replay_machine = machine_description (), recorded_paced = _recorded_paced ( header = header ), ) if options . compare_processing else None ), ) # A bookmarked copy of a version-2 recording replays as version 2 (rule 16) input_capture_format_version = header . get ( INPUT_CAPTURE_FORMAT_HEADER_FIELD ) if isinstance ( input_capture_format_version , int ): format_version = min ( format_version , input_capture_format_version ) self . draws_overlay = not options . headless self . captures_scene_starts = options . captures_scene_starts # Watched, inner frames are not presented: the viewer's outer tick presents the latest self . presents_frames = options . headless self . controls = ReplayControls ( total_frames = self . recording . frame_count , awaiting_start = options . wait_for_start and not options . headless , ) self . viewer = ReplayViewer ( controls = self . controls ) # A bookmarked copy's bookmarks are the viewer's from the start, so S keeps them self . controls . bookmarks = recorded_bookmarks ( frames = frames ) self . bookmarks = BookmarkedCopy ( controls = self . controls , recording_path = options . recording_path , is_bookmarked_copy = BOOKMARKED_COPY_OF_HEADER_FIELD in header , ) # A restarted watched replay rebuilds up to its pause frame (rule 15) self . _rebuild : Rebuild | None = None if options . pause_at_frame is not None and not options . headless : self . _rebuild = Rebuild ( target_frame = max ( options . pause_at_frame , FIRST_PAUSED_FRAME )) self . controls . rebuild_target_frame = self . _rebuild . target_frame if options . viewer_state is not None : # What the viewer had set before the restart (the engine carries the panel over to # the scene manager's debug overlay with the controls') self . controls . speed = options . viewer_state . speed self . controls . debug_overlay . panel = options . viewer_state . debug_panel self . controls . divergence_frame = options . viewer_state . divergence_frame self . _compares_control_events = format_version >= CONTROL_EVENTS_FORMAT_VERSION # Frames ended so far (end_frame calls), after the start frame: the index of the frame # being served (rule 3; a playback starts at a later frame, rule 18) self . _frame_index = options . start_frame # Pumps so far in the current frame: the index of the batch the next pump serves self . _pump_index = 0 # The start frame's earlier internal events still to serve from the recording (rule 18) self . _earlier_internal_events_to_serve = options . earlier_internal_event_count self . _stop_requested = False self . _window_was_closed = False self . _last_batch_origins : list [ str ] = [] # Internal events a held frame drained from the real queue, for the next pump (rule 14) self . _held_internal_events : list [ pygame . event . Event ] = [] # The first difference the current frame's pumps found (reported at end_frame) self . _frame_divergence : Divergence | None = None # One frame_digest per compared frame, kept only when digest_path is set (rule 12) self . _frame_digests : list [ str ] = [] # Joystick instance ids without a stand-in already warned about, and unrepresentable # types already logged self . _warned_joystick_instances : set [ int ] = set () self . _logged_unrepresentable_types : set [ str ] = set () # Only its event pump is used: the one place the real queue is read (rule 2) self . _live_queue = LiveSources ( random_seed = self . random_seed , use_fastevents = options . use_fastevents ) # Real input blocked at SDL from the first drain of the queue until the replay ends or # is uninstalled (rule 2); the snapshot is taken once, so a drain after the end does not # block again. A watched replay leaves the viewer's keys unblocked (rule 14) blocked_event_types = ( REAL_INPUT_EVENT_TYPES if options . headless else tuple ( event_type for event_type in REAL_INPUT_EVENT_TYPES if event_type not in WATCHED_REAL_KEY_EVENT_TYPES ) ) self . _real_input_block = EventTypeBlock ( event_types = blocked_event_types ) self . _has_blocked_real_input = False # A playback from a later frame continues the recording's sprite ids (rule 18) self . _sprite_ids = StableSpriteIds ( recorded_ids = _ids_given_before_start ( frames = frames , start_frame = options . start_frame ) ) self . _snapshot : InputSnapshot = IDLE_INPUT self . _devices = ReplayDeviceRegistry ( descriptors = [ DeviceDescriptor . from_json ( record ) for record in header . get ( DEVICES_HEADER_FIELD , []) ], enumeration_answers = [ EnumerationAnswer . from_json ( record ) for record in header . get ( DEVICE_ENUMERATION_FIELD , []) ], ) # Namespace -> the recorded snapshot a store opened for it starts from self . _save_snapshots : dict [ str , dict [ str , Any ]] = dict ( header . get ( SAVES_HEADER_FIELD , {})) self . _opened_save_namespaces : dict [ str , MemorySaveManager ] = {} if format_version < TRACE_FORMAT_VERSION : LOG . warning ( VERSION_TWO_INPUT_WARNING , format_version ) self . start_input = self . _learn_frames_before_start ( frames = frames ) # Sets frame_bridge and recorded_playback_answers too (declared on the class) self . _begin_frame () @classmethod def from_path ( cls , * , path : Path , options : ReplayOptions = DEFAULT_REPLAY_OPTIONS , ) -> ReplaySources : """Read a recording file into replay sources. A file cut off part way (a killed recorder) replays up to its last complete frame (``recording.is_truncated``; ``announce_replay`` says so once the run will replay it). A file that is not a readable recording raises TraceFormatError (from reading it, or from a header without the seed or start time), a missing one OSError. Args: path: The recording. options: How the replay is run. Returns: The sources. """ read_result = read_trace_result ( path = path ) frames = read_result . trace [ FRAMES_FIELD ] is_truncated = is_cut_off ( read_result = read_result ) header = { name : value for name , value in read_result . trace . items () if name != FRAMES_FIELD } return decoded_replay_sources ( header = header , frames = frames , format_version = read_result . format_version , is_truncated = is_truncated , options = options , ) @property def opened_save_namespaces ( self : Self ) -> Mapping [ str , SaveManager ]: """Every memory store opened so far, by namespace (read-only).""" return MappingProxyType ( self . _opened_save_namespaces ) @property def stop_requested ( self : Self ) -> bool : """True once the replay should end the run. A headless replay stops once it diverged or reached its last frame; any replay stops once the window was closed or (watched) Esc was pressed. """ return self . _stop_requested def on_installed ( self : Self ) -> None : """Own the internal-post tracker while installed (internal events pass through).""" start_tracking_internal_posts () def on_uninstalled ( self : Self ) -> None : """Give up the internal-post tracker and restore the blocked state of real input. A rebuild still running stops following the game's music calls (rule 15). """ stop_tracking_internal_posts () self . _real_input_block . restore () if self . _rebuild is not None : self . _rebuild . stop_following_music () def pump_events ( self : Self , * , real_events : list [ pygame . event . Event ] | None = None ) -> list [ pygame . event . Event ]: """Serve the recording's batch for this pump, merged with live internal events (rule 2). The first drain of the real queue blocks real input at SDL (rule 2), and every later one blocks it again (event managers made mid-run allow their types); a pump given ``real_events`` does not own the queue, so it blocks nothing. A watched replay's real key presses go to its controls (rule 14). Args: real_events: The real batch to filter instead of draining the real queue (a Part 3 playback scope passes the base pump's batch). Returns: The recorded batch in its order (external events from the recording, internal ones as the replayed code posted them again), then any live internal event the recording does not have, then the window's QUIT if it was closed. """ is_first_drain = real_events is None and not self . _has_blocked_real_input live_events = self . _drain_real_queue () if real_events is None else real_events live_internal_events , window_closes = self . _sort_live_events ( live_events = live_events , is_first_drain = is_first_drain ) # Posted but not returned: the queue was cleared or the type is blocked forget_pending_posts () # Posts a held frame found come first: they were queued before this drain (rule 14) live_internal_events = [ * self . _held_internal_events , * live_internal_events ] self . _held_internal_events = [] bridge_events : list [ pygame . event . Event ] = [] bridge_origins : list [ str ] = [] if self . frame_bridge is not None and self . _pump_index == 0 : bridge_events , bridge_origins , live_internal_events = ( self . _resumed_frame_redelivered_events ( live_internal_events = live_internal_events ) ) batch , origins = self . _merged_batch ( live_internal_events = live_internal_events ) batch = [ * bridge_events , * batch ] origins = [ * bridge_origins , * origins ] if self . options . serves_redelivered_events and self . _pump_index == 0 : redelivered , redelivered_origins = self . _start_frame_redelivered_events () batch = [ * redelivered , * batch ] origins = [ * redelivered_origins , * origins ] self . _pump_index += 1 if window_closes : self . _window_was_closed = True batch . append ( window_closes [ - 1 ]) origins . append ( EXTERNAL_ORIGIN ) self . _last_batch_origins = origins return batch def last_batch_origins ( self : Self ) -> list [ str ]: """Return each event's origin in the batch the last pump returned. For a recording made over the replay (``--rebaseline``, rule 17), which records these rather than classify the batch with the internal-post tracker (the pump above has already consumed its pending posts). Returns: ``'external'`` for served recorded events and a window close, ``'internal'`` for passed-through live events. """ return list ( self . _last_batch_origins ) def frame_seconds ( self : Self , * , measured : float ) -> float : """Return the current frame's recorded dt (rule 4). The scene manager asks before frame 0 and after each frame ends, so the first call returns frame 0's dt and each later call the next frame's. Args: measured: The measured start-to-start time. Returns: The recorded dt; ``measured`` past the end of the recording. """ frame = self . _current_frame () if frame is None : return measured return float ( frame [ DT_FIELD ]) def performance_frame_seconds ( self : Self , * , measured : float , frame_seconds : float ) -> float : """Return the frame time FPS events and the performance statistics use (rule 4). Args: measured: The measured start-to-start time. frame_seconds: The frame time ``frame_seconds()`` returned (the recorded dt). Returns: ``frame_seconds`` under ``--replay-fps recorded``, ``measured`` under ``real``. """ if self . options . fps_source == REAL_REPLAY_FPS : return measured return frame_seconds def paced_frame_seconds ( self : Self ) -> float | None : """Return how the frame starting now is paced (rule 13). Returns: 0.0: a headless replay is not paced, and a watched one paces itself in ``hold_frame`` (holding the loop until the frame is due), so the scene manager never waits for it. """ return 0.0 def hold_frame ( self : Self ) -> bool : """Drive the viewer's outer loop: say whether the next inner frame waits (rule 14). Opens the viewer's next outer tick when none is open (sleeping until it is due, then reading the viewer's keys and refreshing the status line), and runs inner frames from the viewer's accumulator (glitchygames/replay/viewer.py). While a restarted replay rebuilds (rule 15) no outer tick opens: frames run unheld, but for one hold every ``REBUILD_PROGRESS_INTERVAL_SECONDS`` of real time, which reads the viewer's keys (Esc and the window's close still end the replay) and presents the progress line. Returns: False when headless (a headless replay never holds), while rebuilding (but at its progress) or when the viewer runs one more inner frame in its open tick; True when the tick closes or the rebuild shows its progress (the loop presents the outer frame and asks again). """ if self . options . headless : return False if self . _rebuild is not None : # Before frame 0's game code: the game's own music pauses are followed from it self . _rebuild . begin () now = measured_seconds () if not self . _rebuild . progress_is_due ( frame_index = self . _frame_index , now = now ): return False self . _run_control_tick ( now = now ) return True # Nothing has run since the last tick closed: its state decides how the viewer waits now = self . viewer . begin_tick ( is_inner_running = self . _is_inner_running ()) if now is not None : self . _run_control_tick ( now = now ) self . viewer . accrue ( now = now , is_inner_running = self . _is_inner_running ()) runs_inner_frame = self . viewer . should_run_inner_frame ( inner_frame_seconds = self . _inner_frame_seconds (), is_inner_over = self . _is_inner_over (), is_first_inner_frame = self . _frame_index == 0 , ) if not runs_inner_frame : # The tick closed: the status line describes the frame about to be presented self . _refresh_status_line () return not runs_inner_frame def draw_overlay ( self : Self , * , surface : pygame . Surface ) -> None : """Draw the watched replay's status bar, banner and start screen (rule 14). What is drawn changes once per control tick (``hold_frame``); it is drawn on every presented frame. Args: surface: The presented frame (never a screenshot or a traced frame). """ self . controls . draw ( surface = surface ) def input_snapshot ( self : Self ) -> InputSnapshot : """Return the current frame's recorded polled input (rule 5). Returns: The snapshot (the last recorded one past the end). """ return self . _snapshot def devices ( self : Self ) -> ReplayDeviceRegistry : """Return the registry of recorded devices (rule 6). Returns: The registry. """ return self . _devices def saves ( self : Self , * , namespace : str ) -> SaveManager : """Open (or return the already opened) memory store for ``namespace`` (rule 7). Args: namespace: The game's app name. Returns: A MemorySaveManager seeded from the recorded snapshot (empty when the recording has none for ``namespace``). """ store = self . _opened_save_namespaces . get ( namespace ) if store is None : store = MemorySaveManager ( app_name = namespace , snapshot = self . _save_snapshots . get ( namespace , {}) ) self . _opened_save_namespaces [ namespace ] = store return store def wall_clock_time ( self : Self ) -> datetime : """Return the recording's start time plus the frame clock (rule 9). Returns: Timezone-aware time. """ return self . _recorded_at + timedelta ( seconds = frame_clock_seconds ()) def control_events_for_frame ( self : Self , * , frame_number : int ) -> list [ ControlEvent ]: """Return the current frame's recorded supervisor actions, to apply again. Args: frame_number: The scene manager's frame number (not used to pick the frame: rule 3). Returns: The recorded control events whose kind is applied again, in order (markers the replayed code records by itself are left out). """ del frame_number frame = self . _current_frame () # Frames run only while the recording has one: a headless replay stops after its last # frame, a watched one holds there (rules 8 and 14) assert frame is not None return [ ControlEvent . from_json ( record ) for record in frame . get ( CONTROL_EVENTS_FIELD , []) if record . get ( KIND_FIELD ) in REAPPLIED_CONTROL_EVENT_KINDS ] def end_frame ( self : Self , * , frame_number : int , dt : float , scene : Scene | None , control_events : list [ ControlEvent ], processing_seconds : float | None = None , ) -> None : """Compare the frame with the recorded one, then move on to the next (rule 8). docs.text: Make replay sources from a decoded recording, refusing a malformed one (rule 1). What the sources decode as they are made (the header's devices, enumeration answers and saves, the frames before the start frame and the start frame itself: their devices, saves, input changes and resume bridge) is checked here, so a malformed recording raises TraceFormatError, which the engine refuses with ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT as it does an unreadable file ( ReplaySources.from_path ), and a playback refuses as it does any recording it cannot play ( playback_replay_sources ). What the sources decode as they are made (the header's devices, enumeration answers and saves, the frames before the start frame and the start frame itself: their devices, saves, input changes and resume bridge) is checked here, so a malformed recording raises TraceFormatError, which the engine refuses with ``ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT`` as it does an unreadable file (``ReplaySources.from_path``), and a playback refuses as it does any recording it cannot play (``playback_replay_sources``). Known limitation: the catch covers the whole ``ReplaySources.__init__``, so a genuine engine bug there that raises AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError or ValueError is reported as a malformed recording (``UNUSABLE_INPUT``, 65), not as ``INTERNAL_ERROR`` (70); the message keeps the original exception (``repr``), and it is chained as the cause. Args: header: The header fields. frames: Every complete recorded frame, decoded. format_version: The file's format version (2 or 3). is_truncated: True when the file was cut off. options: How the replay is run. A recorder over a replay ( --rebaseline ) takes them from the replay, and so does the instant-replay journal (glitchygames/instant_replay.py, rule 4): a watched replay's held frames drain the real queue between pumps, so the posts pending before a pump do not tell them. docs.text: Write a copy of a recording with a breakpoint for each bookmark (rule 16). The recording's header and complete frames are copied as read; for each bookmark N, frame N - 1 gets BOOKMARK_CONTROL_EVENT appended to its control events, unless it already has it, and its newest content hash ( content_hash[0] , glitchygames/recording_history.py) is recomputed to describe the breakpoint. The header gains bookmarked_copy_of (the source's file name, kept from a copy), source_truncated when the source was cut off, and input_capture_format_version when the source is older than format version 3, so the copy replays as its source does. A copy an earlier session saved from the same source keeps its bookmarks: they are added to bookmarks (a copy of another recording is never written over). The copy is written aside, then moved into place ( glitchygames.output_files.write_aside_then_replace ), so destination is never left half written, even when it is recording_path . Parameters: recording_path ( Path ) – The recording to copy (never written, unless it is a bookmarked copy and destination ). bookmarks ( list [ int ] ) – The bookmarked frames ( ReplayControls.bookmarks ), each 1 to the recording's frame count. destination ( Path ) – The copy's path ( bookmarked_copy_path ): a new file or a bookmarked copy. Raises: ValueError – If destination exists but is not a bookmarked copy of recording_path , or a bookmark is outside the recording (nothing is written either way). docs.text: Ghosts: one sprite's recorded path and looks, drawn beside live play (a time-trial ghost). A ghost is appearance, not play (plans/2026-10-19-gameplay-replay.md, section 5.5). The rules: Recording: GhostRecorder(sprite=..., scene=...) is a supervisor (glitchygames/supervision.py); it registers itself with SceneManager().add_supervisor as it is made and removes itself in finish() , which returns the GhostTrack . At each frame's supervisor slot (after the frame's logic and events, before the camera aim and positioning) it keeps one GhostSample : the scene's game_time , the sprite's world_x / world_y , its appearance(sprite) ( default_appearance : animation, frame, horizontal flip and draw offset of an AnimatedSprite ; kept as a read-only copy) and whether the game shows it ( not hidden for a world-space sprite: its visible is the engine's culling, which says where the camera was, not whether the sprite was shown; visible for any other sprite). Only live frames of its scene are sampled: frames whose active scene is the scene it was given (another scene has its own game time), in which that scene's game time advanced (not behind the pause screen, not the frame a resume switches back to it), and never inside a playback scope (a demo or an instant replay plays a rebuilt scene; glitchygames/replay/playback.py). A recorder made while a scope plays (by the rebuilt scene's setup() , say) belongs to the scope: the scene manager removes it when the scope ends (glitchygames/supervision.py), and it samples nothing. A recorder stays registered until finish() , even once its scene is gone: a scene left (for the pause screen, or for another the game comes back from) may return, so the engine cannot tell it is over; a recorder never finished samples nothing more, but is kept (with its scene) until the game calls finish() , typically when the run it records ends. The recorder reads game state only: it draws no randomness, posts no event and records no control event, so recording a ghost changes nothing a --record-trace recording holds or a replay compares. Timing: samples are keyed by Scene.game_time , the sum of the scene's (capped) dt since it started, which stops while the scene is paused. A ghost drawn in a later run of the same scene shows, at each moment, the last sample not after that run's game_time ( GhostTrack.sample_at ), so it lines up with the live run from the scene's start whatever the frame rate, and stands still while the game is paused. With the same dt every frame, the ghost is drawn exactly where the recorded sprite was drawn. Storing: GhostTrack.to_json() / from_json() (frozen pydantic models; unknown fields are refused). The game stores tracks, typically in its saves ( glitchygames.state. open_saves ): a replay serves the saves the recording saw (a sandbox), so the replayed ghost is the recorded one. A track read from anywhere else must be the same file when the session is replayed. Drawing: GhostSprite(track=..., image_for=...) is a world-space sprite ( COORDINATE_SPACE = CoordinateSpace.WORLD ): the engine positions and culls it like any world sprite and is the only writer of its rect's position. The game sets ghost.scene to the scene it adds the ghost to (whose game_time it follows) and adds it to the scene's all_sprites . Its world_x , world_y and draw_offset are read from the track at the scene's current game_time whenever they are read, and that read brings its image and rect size up to date, so the engine's positioning (which runs before update() ) places and culls this frame's sample, never the last frame's. Its image is image_for(sample) as a translucent copy ( alpha ), made once per distinct appearance (keyed by the appearance's JSON), and the rect takes its size (its top-left stays the engine's). With nothing to show (no scene, before the track's first sample, or a sample that is not visible) its image is empty (0 x 0), which the engine's culling hides ( visible 0). hidden is the game's own flag only, as for every world sprite (set hidden = True to hide it, never visible = False ), so saving and restoring it is safe. It has no hitbox: never add it to a collision group. In traces: a ghost in all_sprites is sampled like every sprite (its rect and visible ), and it is deterministic: its track comes from saves (rule 4) and its position from the replayed game_time , so a session with a ghost replays without divergence. Inside an instant replay the rebuilt scene adds its own ghost as the live scene did (from the sandboxed saves), following its own game_time .

docs.text: A supervisor that samples one sprite once per live frame of its scene (module rules 1-2). Source code in glitchygames/replay/ghosts.py 270 271 272 273 274 275 276 277 278 279 280 281 282 283 284 285 286 287 288 289 290 291 292 293 294 295 296 297 298 299 300 301 302 303 304 305 306 307 308 309 310 311 312 313 314 315 316 317 318 319 320 321 322 323 324 325 326 327 328 329 330 331 332 333 334 335 336 337 338 class GhostRecorder : """A supervisor that samples one sprite once per live frame of its scene (module rules 1-2).""" def __init__ ( self : Self , * , sprite : WorldPositioned , scene : Scene , appearance : Callable [[ object ], dict [ str , Any ]] = default_appearance , ) -> None : """Start recording ``sprite``: register with the scene manager's supervisor slot. Args: sprite: The sprite to record (it has world_x and world_y). scene: The scene the sprite plays in: only its frames are sampled, keyed by its game time. appearance: Returns the JSON-safe looks of the sprite for each sample. """ self . _sprite = sprite self . _scene = scene self . _appearance = appearance self . _samples : list [ GhostSample ] = [] self . _track : GhostTrack | None = None SceneManager () . add_supervisor ( supervisor = self ) def on_frame ( self : Self , * , frame_number : int , scene : Scene | None ) -> None : """Sample the sprite, if this frame ran the recorded scene's logic live. Args: frame_number: The frame being run (unused: samples are keyed by game time). scene: The active scene at the supervisor slot. """ del frame_number # A supervisor earlier in the slot may have finished this recorder this frame if self . _track is not None or scene is not self . _scene : return if SceneManager () . in_playback_scope : return game_seconds = self . _scene . game_time if self . _samples and game_seconds <= self . _samples [ - 1 ] . game_seconds : return sprite = self . _sprite if is_world_positioned ( sprite ): shown = not getattr ( sprite , 'hidden' , False ) else : shown = bool ( getattr ( sprite , 'visible' , True )) self . _samples . append ( GhostSample ( game_seconds = game_seconds , world_x = sprite . world_x , world_y = sprite . world_y , appearance = self . _appearance ( sprite ), visible = shown , ) ) def finish ( self : Self ) -> GhostTrack : """Stop recording: leave the supervisor slot and return the track (the same each call). Returns: The recorded track. """ if self . _track is None : SceneManager () . remove_supervisor ( supervisor = self ) self . _track = GhostTrack ( samples = tuple ( self . _samples )) return self . _track

Surface ] = {} self . _empty_image = pygame . Surface (( 0 , 0 )) self . image = self . _empty_image self . rect = self . _empty_image . get_rect () def _current_sample ( self : Self ) -> GhostSample | None : """Return the sample for the scene's current game time, showing its image. Source code in glitchygames/replay/ghosts.py 148 149 150 151 152 153 154 155 156 157 158 159 160 161 162 163 164 165 166 167 168 169 170 171 172 173 174 175 176 177 178 179 180 181 182 183 184 185 186 187 188 189 190 191 192 193 194 195 196 197 198 199 200 201 202 203 204 205 206 207 208 209 210 211 212 class GhostTrack ( BaseModel ): """A recorded sprite's samples, in game-time order.""" model_config = ConfigDict ( frozen = True , extra = 'forbid' ) samples : tuple [ GhostSample , ... ] @model_validator ( mode = 'after' ) def _check_time_order ( self : Self ) -> Self : """Refuse samples whose game times go backwards (sample_at searches them). Returns: The track. Raises: ValueError: If a sample's game time is earlier than the one before it. """ for earlier , later in zip ( self . samples , self . samples [ 1 :], strict = False ): if later . game_seconds < earlier . game_seconds : message = ( f 'Ghost samples must be in time order: { later . game_seconds } follows ' f ' { earlier . game_seconds } ' ) raise ValueError ( message ) return self def sample_at ( self : Self , * , game_seconds : float ) -> GhostSample | None : """Return the last sample taken at or before a game time. Args: game_seconds: The game time of the scene the ghost is drawn in. Returns: The sample, or None before the first sample (or for an empty track). """ index = bisect . bisect_right ( self . samples , game_seconds , key = lambda sample : sample . game_seconds ) if index == 0 : return None return self . samples [ index - 1 ] def to_json ( self : Self ) -> dict [ str , Any ]: """Return the track as plain JSON types (for saves). Returns: ``{'samples': [...]}``, each sample a dict of its fields. """ return self . model_dump ( mode = 'json' ) @classmethod def from_json ( cls , record : dict [ str , Any ]) -> GhostTrack : """Read a track written by ``to_json``. Args: record: The JSON record. Returns: The track. """ return cls . model_validate ( record )

docs.text: Block real input at SDL while recorded input is served, then put the earlier state back. A replay (glitchygames/replay/driver.py) serves every external event from its recording, so real input, device and window events are blocked at SDL ( pygame.event.set_blocked ): they never enter the queue. EventTypeBlock records each type's blocked state before blocking it and restores exactly that state, so a type a game had already blocked stays blocked. Event managers made mid-run (a scene's widgets) call pygame.event.set_allowed , so the replay blocks the types again on every pump ( reassert ). Part 3's playback scope can reuse it. Blocking a type also refuses posts of it ( pygame.event.post returns False), including the game's own: game code that fakes input by posting, say, KEYDOWN loses those posts during a replay. The engine's own posts are QUIT and custom types, which are never blocked.

docs.text: Blocks event types at SDL and restores each one's blocked state at block() time. restore() returns every type to the state it had when block() ran, overriding any pygame.event.set_allowed or set_blocked calls made for those types in between. Attributes: event_types ( tuple [ int , ...] ) – The types block() blocks. Source code in glitchygames/replay/input_blocking.py 108 109 110 111 112 113 114 115 116 117 118 119 120 121 122 123 124 125 126 127 128 129 130 131 132 133 134 135 136 137 138 139 140 141 142 143 144 145 146 147 148 149 150 151 152 153 154 155 156 157 158 159 160 161 162 163 164 165 class EventTypeBlock : """Blocks event types at SDL and restores each one's blocked state at ``block()`` time. ``restore()`` returns every type to the state it had when ``block()`` ran, overriding any ``pygame.event.set_allowed`` or ``set_blocked`` calls made for those types in between. Attributes: event_types: The types ``block()`` blocks. """ def __init__ ( self : Self , * , event_types : Iterable [ int ]) -> None : """Prepare to block ``event_types`` (nothing is blocked until ``block()``). Args: event_types: The event types to block. """ self . event_types : tuple [ int , ... ] = tuple ( event_types ) # Type -> whether it was blocked before block(); None while not active self . _blocked_before : dict [ int , bool ] | None = None @property def is_active ( self : Self ) -> bool : """True between ``block()`` and ``restore()``.""" return self . _blocked_before is not None def block ( self : Self ) -> None : """Record each type's blocked state, then block every type (a no-op while active).""" if self . is_active : return self . _blocked_before = { event_type : pygame . event . get_blocked ( event_type ) for event_type in self . event_types } pygame . event . set_blocked ( list ( self . event_types )) def reassert ( self : Self ) -> None : """Block every type again, keeping the snapshot ``block()`` took (a no-op unless active). Undoes ``pygame.event.set_allowed`` calls made since (an event manager made mid-run). """ if self . _blocked_before is None : return pygame . event . set_blocked ( list ( self . event_types )) def restore ( self : Self ) -> None : """Return each type to its state at ``block()`` time (a no-op unless active). Types blocked then stay blocked; the others are unblocked, whatever was set in between. """ if self . _blocked_before is None : return pygame . event . set_allowed ([ event_type for event_type , was_blocked in self . _blocked_before . items () if not was_blocked ]) self . _blocked_before = None

docs.text: In-game playback: a running game plays a recording to a rebuilt scene, then goes on. Demos and instant replays run inside a playback scope, not a new engine run (plans/2026-10-19-gameplay-replay.md, section 5.2). The rules: Starting ( start_playback ; start_playback_from_recording reads a file first): the frame played first ( PlaybackOptions.start_frame ) must hold a scene_start (glitchygames/scene_start.py) with its first logic frame (rule 7 there: a recording writes a start on the scene's first logic frame, so the start's frame is where its logic began), and its scene class must be found among the loaded Scene subclasses ( find_scene_class : by module and qualified name, else, where the modules cannot be compared (none recorded, or __main__ on either side), by a name no other such scene shares); otherwise nothing starts (logged; False), as for a recording that cannot be replayed (a malformed one included). The replay sources are made ( playback_replay_sources , rule 18 of glitchygames/replay/driver.py) and the scope is requested ( SceneManager. request_playback ): the scene manager enters it at the start of the next frame, so the rebuilt scene's first frame is a whole frame, as recorded, and the frame that asked ends on the live doors. A request made while a transition plays waits for its end. A request made in a frame whose end switches scenes ( next_scene ) is dropped, logged: the scene to return to has gone. Scopes do not nest: inside a scope, a request is answered with the answer the frame being played recorded (an instant-replay journal's playback_answers ) and requests nothing, or, without one, refused ( answered_playback_request ; glitchygames/instant_replay.py, rule 8). Entering ( SceneManager._enter_playback ): the random streams, the frame clock, the FPS event timer and the scene manager's previous_scene are saved ( PlaybackRequest.begin_session ); the live scene is stashed without cleanup() ; PlaybackSources are pushed on top of the installed doors ( push_scoped_sources ; glitchygames/sources.py); a playback control event is recorded (a marker: replaying the session starts the scope again from the recorded input, so it is compared, never applied again); the scene is rebuilt ( rebuild_scene ) and made active as a switch would, a transition's arrival step is repeated for a scene that arrived by one; then the streams, the frame clock and the FPS event timer are set as the scene's first logic frame began, the frame takes the recording's dt, and the current polled input becomes the recording's before that frame (idle before frame 0), so the live input never leaks in. Frames: PlaybackSources serve the recording to the scene (rule 5) and the scene manager runs every frame as always, paced and presented by the installed doors (a demo plays at the game's speed), but for the fast-forwarded frames (rule 6). Ending: after each frame, the scope ends when its doors found a reason ( PlaybackSources.end_reason ): the player's press ( exit_on_input : any key or button, PLAYBACK_EXIT_EVENT_TYPES ), the recording's quit (its window's QUIT or the playback scene's own quit_game() : the scope ends, the game does not quit), the game's request ( SceneManager.end_playback , 'ended_by_game' : from a supervisor, the scope ends once that frame ended; between frames, at once; from the played scene's own code, ignored, as its original call did nothing), or the recording's end or divergence (the replay stops there; a playback never pauses). An error in the scope's part of a frame (its frame, the comparison, or entering) ends it too, logged ( SceneManager._run_frame contains it); an error of the installed doors (a session recorder that cannot write) propagates as it would outside a scope. The run's end ( SceneManager.terminate , after the player's QUIT) ends a scope in progress first and drops a requested one, so the live scene is the one torn down. Ending ( SceneManager._exit_playback ) keeps the replay's result ( SceneManager.last_playback_result ) and a PlaybackOutcome ( SceneManager.last_playback_outcome : the kind, the reason and the frames played), cleans up the playback's scene, removes every supervisor and control event handler the scope's code added while it played (the rebuilt scene's setup(), event handlers or cleanup() may add one, a ghost recorder say: SceneManager.add_supervisor gives it to the scope; those added before the scope began, or by the live game's own supervisors and handlers while it played, stay; SceneManager.in_playback_scope , true while the scoped doors are pushed, is the one answer to "is a scope playing"), pops the scoped doors, restores the streams, the frame clock, the FPS event timer, the scene manager's previous_scene , its rumble controller (rule 8) and the live polled input (the installed doors' latest snapshot), posts again the live game's posts the scope drained and hands back the player's held events (rule 5), drops the playback scene's own posts still queued (made after its frame's last pump: in update() , an event handler, a supervisor or handler the scope owns, its cleanup; sources.discard_scope_posts : they stop being pending posts, and the live doors' next read of SDL's queue loses them before a recording, the instant-replay journal or the game sees the batch; a replay of the session drops them the same way as its playback scene posts them again), posts again, in posting order, the posts the live game's own supervisors and handlers made while it played ( held_live_game_posts and those still queued, made in its last frame: a supervisor that calls end_playback() and then posts for the live game, say; the queued copies are dropped as the scope's are, so each arrives once, after the held events, at the live doors' next pump; pending then, a later instant replay across the scope serves them uncompared as its resume bridge's earlier events), then makes the live scene active again exactly as it was (no setup() again: only its snap mode, event proxies, caption and a full redraw), or switches to then when that is another scene. The frame that ends the scope still finishes afterwards, so the restored live frame clock resumes one frame later (it advances by that frame's dt). The scoped doors ( PlaybackSources ): pump_events : the installed doors pump once per pump of the frame (the real queue live; the session's recorded batch when the session is replayed, so the exit press replays too). Their batch is sorted with the internal-post tracker. The player's QUIT (and one the live game posted) is kept: it quits the game. Internal events, the playback scene's own posts, go to the replay ( ReplaySources.pump_events(real_events=...) ), which matches them with the recorded ones. Internal events posted before the scope began (the live game's last FPS event, say: they are the live game's, and would be divergences of the recording's first frame) are held, as are the external events the live game must not lose (releases, device and window events, PLAYBACK_HELD_EVENT_TYPES ): one list ( held_live_events ), in the order they were pumped, each with its origin, delivered in that order before the first pump after the scope ( sources.redeliver_events ; a recording writes them into that frame's redelivered_events ). Events still waiting to be redelivered when a scope begins (a demo that ended into a scene starting the next one) are taken into the new scope's list first, so they reach the live game, never a playback scene. When the run ends during a scope ( terminate ) they are dropped: no frame follows to deliver them. The posts the live game's own supervisors and control event handlers make while the scope plays ( recording.live_game_posts : post_event marks them while SceneManager runs live code in a scope, rule 4; the played recording never held them) are held apart ( held_live_game_posts ) and posted again as the scope ends (rule 4). The live game's input posts ( recording.post_input_event : a supervisor or tool standing in for the player) of an SDL type (below USEREVENT ), made during the scope or before it, are the player's input (BUGS.md #196): a press reaches the exit check (it ends a demo), releases, device and window events are held with the player's ( held_live_events , external), and the rest reach nothing. A replay of the session runs without the poster and serves those events from the recording as the player's, so the two agree. Its input posts of a type SDL never generates (no player makes one: a game event, a menu event, any custom_type() ) are held as its other posts are, and posted (or redelivered) as input again after the scope. A replay of the session serves those from the recording too (external), and the scope holds a served event of such a type that matches no post the same way, told by its recorded origin ( replayed_batch_origins : the type alone would call it internal), so it reaches the live game after the scope there as well. The rule: a supervisor may post any event ( post_input_event ); input of an SDL type during a scope counts as the player's; everything else reaches the game (after the scope if one is playing), live and replayed alike. The scope's code's own input posts (a supervisor the played scene added again) are dropped: the recording holds them as external and the replay serves them, so each arrives once. External events reach only the exit check, never the scene; presses and motion are dropped. The batch is the replay's (recorded external events, matched internal ones) without any QUIT (a QUIT in it ends the scope: recording_quit ), then the kept QUIT. input_snapshot : the installed doors' snapshot is read (a recording of the session records the player's polled input; it is kept as last_base_snapshot ), the replay's is returned. frame_seconds : the replay's (the recording's dt; past its end, the installed doors' measurement), asked after the installed doors were asked as always. Their answer is kept ( installed_frame_seconds ) for their end_frame . saves , devices , wall_clock_time , random_seed , opened_save_namespaces : the replay's (saves are a sandbox seeded from the scene start's save view: real saves are never touched). control_events_for_frame : the installed doors' (a replay of the session re-applies its breakpoints on the scope's frames too); the played recording's re-applied control events are never applied again (they were applied in the session that recorded them) and never compared (glitchygames/replay/driver.py, rule 8). end_frame is compare_frame (the replay compares the frame, its playback marker left out: the recording never holds it), then the installed doors' end_frame (a recording of the session writes it; glitchygames/recording.py, Playback scopes) with their own frame time ( installed_frame_seconds ), not the played recording's dt the frame ran with: the scope's first frame's time was read as the live frame before it ended, on the installed doors, and advanced the live frame clock and FPS event timer there, so a replay of the session must be served that time as that frame ends (BUGS.md #196). The scene manager calls the two itself, so only the comparison's errors end the scope. captures_scene_starts is True; stop_requested , pacing, holding, presenting and the overlay are the installed doors' (the scope never stops the run), except while fast-forwarding (rule 6). Fast-forward ( PlaybackOptions.fast_forward_frames ): the scope's first N frames run in full but unseen and unheard. While PlaybackSources.is_fast_forwarding (fewer frames compared than N), presents_frames is False and paced_frame_seconds() is 0.0, the doors a headless replay uses (the scene manager neither presents nor waits; the next presented frame updates the whole display), and after each such frame every sound it started is stopped and music is paused ( FrameSilencer , glitchygames/replay/silence.py, the code path a restarted replay's rebuild uses; it follows the game's own music pauses from the scope's start, and the live game's sounds playing then play on, live voices aside). After the Nth frame the silence ends (music the silencer paused plays on, unless the game paused it) and the frames play as rule 3 says, heard as the game plays them; so does a scope that ends during the fast-forward. Music is the one mixer's: the scope neither saves nor restores it, so music the playback's scene starts or stops is the live game's too. The scope's first frame is paced as the live doors pace it (the loop asks before the frame enters the scope). None of this changes what a frame does, so a recording or replay of the session (watched or headless) is unchanged. Instant replay ( SceneManager.instant_replay , start_instant_replay ): the active scene's instant-replay journal (glitchygames/instant_replay.py) plays in a scope of kind 'instant' from its start_frame , returning to the scene shown (the journal's scene, or the pause screen presenting it), with no exit on input: the player's presses reach nothing, and the game decides when it ends (the journal's end, or SceneManager.end_playback from a supervisor, which reads the player's polled input from SceneManager.playback_player_input ). The frames before the last Scene.INSTANT_REPLAY_SECONDS of frame time are fast-forwarded ( fast_forward_frame_count ); the rest are shown at the game's pace. Frame time, not game time: the shown part takes that long to watch, a paused stretch in it included. Refused (False, nothing starts) when the scene keeps no journal (it does not offer instant replay, its first logic frame has not run, or a scope plays) or the journal holds more frame time than Scene.MAX_INSTANT_REPLAY_FAST_FORWARD_SECONDS . The request is answered as any playback request is (rule 1: a playback of the journal gets the recorded answer and requests nothing), so a scene that asks after every goal plays back across its earlier replays. The journal's recording is taken as the request is made: the frame that asks is not in it (it ends live, before the scope begins). Rumble and live voices: a playback never rumbles the player's real controllers, neither while fast-forwarding nor in the frames it shows (a demo's crash buzzing the player's hands would be the playback's, not the game's). While a scope plays, SceneManager.rumble is a rumble controller of its own (the playback scene's pulses, sustained levels and shakes go there and reach no device); the live game's controller waits untouched and is back when the scope ends, so a playback's pulse never carries into live play. The live scene's synth voices (and those of the scene the scope returns to, and of the previous scene as it began: the game behind a pause screen an instant replay began from) pause behind the scope and play on after it ( LiveAudio.update 's paused_owners ), even when the playback's own scene switches change previous_scene ; the playback scene's own voices end with it. Limits: a live supervisor that posts with post_event (the game's own posts, which a replay expects the replayed code to make again) during a scope makes a session that a --replay-trace replay without that supervisor cannot match. Supervisors post with post_input_event , which replays without them, whatever the event's type (rule 5). A scope that fast-forwards inside a restarted replay's rebuild silences on top of the rebuild's silence: the end of its fast-forward may resume music during the rebuild (which pauses it again after the next frame). A scene must be rebuildable from its start ( Scene.replay_arguments ). Of a scene that arrived by a transition, the arrival step is repeated, but the events the ride delivered to it (releases, window and device events) are not: a scene they change diverges. The first logic frame's earlier posts are counted from the internal-post tracker, so they are exact while posts are tracked (while recording or replaying, and from the first setup of a scene that keeps an instant-replay journal: glitchygames/instant_replay.py, whose JournalRecording a scope plays from its start_frame ). A --record-trace recording of a session that played a scope cannot itself be played in-game from a frame inside or after that scope: a recorder writes no playback_answers or resume_bridge (only an instant-replay journal does), so its scene's playback requests and its resumption after the scope are not known (it replays exactly with --replay-trace , which runs the scope again). Rumble in joystick mode asks the devices door for the joysticks (glitchygames/input/rumble.py); inside a scope each send still asks the scope's door, with a device cache of its own, and then sends to no device (rule 8), so the played recording's answers are taken as it gave them. The scope's rumble controller starts fresh, though: a rumble the live game sent before the played scene began, still running when it was recorded, is not known to it, so its sends (and the counts they ask) can fall on other frames than the recording's; that matters only when the played recording's joystick count changed part way.

Attributes: base – The installed doors underneath (live, recording or a replay of the session). replay – The replay serving the recording to the playback's scene. exit_on_input – True when any key or button press ends the scope. fast_forward_frames – How many of the scope's first frames run unpresented, unpaced and silent (rule 6). is_fast_forwarding – True while the frame running (or about to run) is one of them: fewer frames compared than fast_forward_frames . exit_requested – True once such a press arrived. recording_quit – True once the recording asked to quit (its window's QUIT, or the playback scene's own quit_game() ): the scope ends, the game does not quit. captures_scene_starts – True: scenes built inside the scope capture their starts. random_seed – The recording's master seed. frames_played – How many frames the replay compared so far. end_reason ( PlaybackEndReason | None ) – Why the scope should end now, or None while it plays on: the first found of the player's exit press ( 'exit_input' ) and the recording's quit ( 'recording_quit' ), found by the frame's pumps, the game's request ( 'ended_by_game' , set by SceneManager.end_playback ), then the replay's end ( 'end_of_recording' , 'truncated' or 'diverged' ), found by compare_frame . last_base_snapshot ( InputSnapshot ) – The installed doors' latest polled input (the live input as the scope began, then each frame's): the live game's input when the scope ends. held_live_events ( list [ RedeliveredEvent ] ) – The live game's events the scope's pumps drained and held, each with its origin, in pump order: its own posts made before the scope (internal) and the player's releases, device and window events (external, PLAYBACK_HELD_EVENT_TYPES ; the live game's input posts of those types among them). Delivered before the first pump after the scope. input_posts_at_pump ( list [ tuple [ int , dict [ str , Any ]]] ) – The pending posts that were input posts ( recording.post_input_event ) as the current pump began, noted before the installed doors pump: a replay's pump (a session replayed) forgets the tracker's posts, their input marks included, once it has sorted its batch. held_live_game_posts ( list [ tuple [ Event , bool ]] ) – The posts the live game's own supervisors and handlers made during the scope ( recording.live_game_posts ) that the scope's pumps drained, in pump order, each with whether it was an input post ( recording.post_input_event ; only of a type SDL never generates: an SDL type's is the player's input, rule 5). docs.text: Answer a playback request as recorded inside a scope, else make it and keep its answer. The scene's code gets the same answers when its instant-replay journal is played back (glitchygames/instant_replay.py, rule 8): live, the answer is kept in the journal's frame ( SceneManager.note_playback_answer ); inside a scope playing the journal, the frame's recorded answer is returned ( SceneManager.recorded_playback_answer ) and the request is not made (scopes do not nest). Inside a scope whose recording holds no answer (a demo), the request is made, and refused as a nested scope. Parameters: manager ( SceneManager ) – The running scene manager. request ( Callable [[], bool ] ) – Makes the request; returns whether a scope will begin. Returns: bool – The answer. Source code in glitchygames/replay/playback.py 1146 1147 1148 1149 1150 1151 1152 1153 1154 1155 1156 1157 1158 1159 1160 1161 1162 1163 1164 1165 1166 1167 1168 1169 def answered_playback_request ( * , manager : SceneManager , request : Callable [[], bool ]) -> bool : """Answer a playback request as recorded inside a scope, else make it and keep its answer. The scene's code gets the same answers when its instant-replay journal is played back (glitchygames/instant_replay.py, rule 8): live, the answer is kept in the journal's frame (``SceneManager.note_playback_answer``); inside a scope playing the journal, the frame's recorded answer is returned (``SceneManager.recorded_playback_answer``) and the request is not made (scopes do not nest). Inside a scope whose recording holds no answer (a demo), the request is made, and refused as a nested scope. Args: manager: The running scene manager. request: Makes the request; returns whether a scope will begin. Returns: The answer. """ recorded_answer = manager . recorded_playback_answer () if recorded_answer is not None : return recorded_answer granted = request () manager . note_playback_answer ( granted = granted ) return granted

docs.text: Return how many frames an instant replay fast-forwards before the seconds it shows. A frame is shown when the frame time from its start to the recording's end (its dt and every later frame's, summed exactly, then rounded once to a float) is at most shown_seconds ; every earlier frame from start_frame is fast-forwarded (rule 7). So ten frames of dt d are shown for shown_seconds 10 * d, whatever float rounding a running sum would add. Parameters: frames ( Sequence [ dict [ str , Any ]] ) – The recording's decoded frames. start_frame ( int ) – The frame the playback starts at. shown_seconds ( float ) – The frame time to show ( Scene.INSTANT_REPLAY_SECONDS ). Returns: int – The number of frames, from start_frame , to fast-forward. Source code in glitchygames/replay/playback.py 1220 1221 1222 1223 1224 1225 1226 1227 1228 1229 1230 1231 1232 1233 1234 1235 1236 1237 1238 1239 1240 1241 1242 1243 1244 1245 1246 1247 def fast_forward_frame_count ( * , frames : Sequence [ dict [ str , Any ]], start_frame : int , shown_seconds : float ) -> int : """Return how many frames an instant replay fast-forwards before the seconds it shows. A frame is shown when the frame time from its start to the recording's end (its ``dt`` and every later frame's, summed exactly, then rounded once to a float) is at most ``shown_seconds``; every earlier frame from ``start_frame`` is fast-forwarded (rule 7). So ten frames of ``dt`` d are shown for ``shown_seconds`` 10 * d, whatever float rounding a running sum would add. Args: frames: The recording's decoded frames. start_frame: The frame the playback starts at. shown_seconds: The frame time to show (``Scene.INSTANT_REPLAY_SECONDS``). Returns: The number of frames, from ``start_frame``, to fast-forward. """ first_shown_frame = len ( frames ) seconds_to_end = Fraction ( 0 ) for frame_index in range ( len ( frames ) - 1 , start_frame - 1 , - 1 ): seconds_to_end += Fraction ( frames [ frame_index ][ DT_FIELD ]) if float ( seconds_to_end ) > shown_seconds : break first_shown_frame = frame_index return first_shown_frame - start_frame

docs.text: Return the loaded Scene subclass a start names (rule 1). Only loaded classes are searched: nothing is imported from recording data. The class defined in module with the qualified name name is taken when exactly one is loaded. Otherwise a class is taken by its qualified name alone only where the modules cannot be compared, as check_recorded_game decides for a recording's game: no module recorded, or a game run as a script ( __main__ ) on either side; then the one such class is taken and several are refused. A class of that name from another module is another game's scene: refused. Parameters: name ( str ) – A class's qualified name ( SceneStart.scene_class ). module ( str | None , default: None ) – The module it is defined in ( SceneStart.scene_module ), or None. Returns: type [ Scene ] | None – The class, or None when no loaded subclass matches or several match by name alone type [ Scene ] | None – (logged).
